title: Forward kinematics, Jacobians and inverse kinematics
text: robot_ik() solves \min_q e(q)^\top W e(q) = \|W^{1/2} e(q)\|^2, e stacks position error rotation-vector orientation error W = \operatorname{diag}(\text{weights}). Three methods available: "levenberg_marquardt" (default): damping scaled largest diagonal entry J^\top W J, adapted accepted rejected step. "damped_least_squares": fixed damping \lambda, robust near singularities. "pseudoinverse": Gauss-Newton backtracking. Steps limited max_step radians meters. Joint limits enforced projection, joints pushed limit frozen step (active set) others keep moving. run converge, restarts (default 5) runs start random configurations drawn fixed seed, results reproducible global random state untouched. Inverse kinematics rarely unique. returned solution depends initial guess: Unreachable targets reported, hidden. solver returns closest configuration found, converged = FALSE, reach bound: Weights select components matter. planar arm control six, x y weighted. 6 DOF arm, zero weight yaw row ask position two tilt angles.

title: Occupancy grids, grid planning and pose graph SLAM
text: pose graph one node per robot pose one edge per relative pose measurement z_{ij} (pose node j frame node ) information matrix \Omega_{ij}. Odometry adds edges consecutive nodes; loop closures add edges distant ones. Optimization solves \min_{x_1, \ldots, x_n} \sum_{(, j)} e_{ij}^\top \Omega_{ij} e_{ij}, \qquad e_{ij} = \begin{pmatrix} R_z^\top\left(R_i^\top (t_j - t_i) - t_z\right) \\ \operatorname{wrap}(\theta_j - \theta_i - \theta_z) \end{pmatrix}, Gauss-Newton steps, Levenberg-Marquardt damping, analytic Jacobians sparse normal-equation solve. first node fixed remove gauge freedom.  plot method draws graph, loop closures dashed:
code: # A robot drives around a square twice; odometry drifts in heading. set.seed(3) steps <- rep(c(rep(c(1, 0, 0), 3), c(1, 0, pi / 2)), 8) steps <- matrix(steps, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE) truth <- matrix(0, nrow(steps) + 1, 3) odom <- truth compose <- function(x, z) {   c(x[1] + cos(x[3]) * z[1] - sin(x[3]) * z[2],     x[2] + sin(x[3]) * z[1] + cos(x[3]) * z[2], wrap_angle(x[3] + z[3])) } noisy <- steps noisy[, 3] <- noisy[, 3] + rnorm(nrow(steps), 0, 0.03) noisy[, 1] <- noisy[, 1] + rnorm(nrow(steps), 0, 0.02) for (k in seq_len(nrow(steps))) {   truth[k + 1, ] <- compose(truth[k, ], steps[k, ])   odom[k + 1, ] <- compose(odom[k, ], noisy[k, ]) } g <- robot_pose_graph(odom) for (k in seq_len(nrow(steps))) {   g <- pose_graph_add_edge(g, k, k + 1, noisy[k, ], diag(c(100, 100, 400))) } # Loop closures: the robot recognizes places it visited one lap earlier. for (k in 1:16) {   g <- pose_graph_add_edge(g, k, k + 16, c(0, 0, 0), diag(c(400, 400, 1000))) } res <- pose_graph_optimize(g) res$converged #> [1] TRUE res$iterations #> [1] 5 signif(res$cost, 3) #> [1] 763.00   6.08   4.64   4.64   4.64 plot(odom[, 1:2], type = "l", col = "grey50", lty = 2, asp = 1,      xlab = "x (m)", ylab = "y (m)") lines(truth[, 1:2], lwd = 3, col = "grey80") lines(res$graph$nodes[, 1:2], col = "firebrick", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("ground truth", "odometry", "optimized"),        col = c("grey80", "grey50", "firebrick"), lty = c(1, 2, 1), lwd = c(3, 1, 2), bty = "n") plot(res$graph)
